title: Shipped files name hv's non-public projects: make them neutral, with a guard whose list does not ship (ST0010 Q5)
body:
hv ruled on 2026-10-27 (vc decision 78, ST0010's Q5, as vc recommended): the public snapshot names Intent, Molt and Utilz, which are public, and no other project of hv's. Shipped files name Gtools, Laksa, Lamplight, Conflab, Baize, Prolix, Prodinfra, Riffle, Cdtempl and the Arca crates, none of which is public. Most of these sit in test comments recording where a case was measured. The rest are in README.md, docs/migration.md, docs/configuration.md, .github/workflows/tests.yml and the release notes (CHANGELOG.md and RELEASES/). A name that resolves to nothing public tells a reader nothing. The release notes ship once this is done (Q6).

## Measured

On main at 4ccfde65, `git grep -w` over the shipped list (tests/shipped.paths, with fleet's files excluded). Per area:
- bin/ and lib/: Intent alone.
- tests: Utilz, Gtools, Intent, Laksa, Lamplight, Conflab, Baize, Prolix, Prodinfra, Riffle, Cdtempl and Arca.
- docs and README: Molt, Utilz, Intent, Laksa, Lamplight, Conflab, Baize and Arca.
- the notes: Molt, Utilz, Gtools, Intent, Laksa, Lamplight, Conflab, Baize, Prolix, Prodinfra and Cdtempl.
- .github and packaging: Molt, Utilz, Intent and Cdtempl.

tests/unit/workroom.bats declares that it does not read a name in prose, so nothing guards this today.

## Fix

- **In main,** each non-public name in a shipped file becomes a neutral phrase that keeps the technical point (eg "one Elixir project", "a project whose version lives in mix.exs", "a Rust crate's CLI"). The release notes get the same treatment.
- **A guard keeps the names out:** a tree scan over tests/shipped.paths that refuses a listed name in a shipped file, naming its file and line.
- **The guard's list of names does not ship.** It is held in a workroom path outside the shipped list, so the public tree carries the guard and not the names. When the list is absent, the guard says so rather than read as clean.
- **Intent, Molt and Utilz stay.**

## Done when

1. No shipped file names a project of hv's other than Intent, Molt and Utilz, by the guard's scan over the workroom.
2. The guard reads the same list workroom.bats reads, and names each file and line it refuses. Its list of names is outside the shipped list. In a tree without the list, it says it read none.
3. Each replacement keeps its comment's technical reason, which vc reads in the diff.
4. The landing suite passes under BSD and GNU with the tree scans and help, and CI is green on the pushed head.

## Resolution

Fixed at 413c12f281e61c59b78defdcaabc0518323ca838, landed on main by vc with the rest of C (fb66b479..7565e2a2) on hv's GO of 29 Oct, as cc banked it. No shipped file names a project of hv's but Intent, Molt and Utilz (hv's Q5, vc decision 78), and a workroom arm refuses the names, read from a list that does not ship.

- **Prose.** Each non-public name in prose becomes a neutral phrase that keeps its comment's technical reason: "one consumer", "a consuming project", "an infra user", "one Elixir consumer", "the field case", and `<project>`, `<alias>` and `<family>` where a line spelt a path or a task. Intent, Molt and Utilz stay.
- **Fixture data.** Each name in fixture data becomes a neutral fixture name, one per project in each file, and each arm checks what it checked before: myapp (myappd, MYAPP_ROOT, MYAPP_IEX), shop (Shop.MixProject, shop.example, shop-app), webapp, chatapp, acme_cli and acme.cli (ACME_STYLE), and Notebook. infra-profile.bats's two fixture handles become gamma and delta, with the same verdicts. README.md and docs/migration.md take myproject, the README's own example, and the migration table is re-padded to it. fullcycle.bats's 0148 arm drops the name from its title, and its (0148) tag stays.
- **The release notes** keep every entry's facts and change only the name, and CHANGELOG.md takes the same text on the same lines, so it is still the view of RELEASES/ that `release notes` renders.
- **The list.** intent/llm/unshipped-names holds the names, one a line with `#` comments: every project of hv's but Intent, Molt and Utilz. It is under intent/, which tests/shipped.paths leaves out, so the names never ship.
- **The guard.** workroom.bats's names arm reads the list through `_workroom_names` (pathlist_specs, then one word of ASCII letters and digits a line, or rc 2) and refuses each name in any shipped line, in any case, as a whole word between characters that are not letters or digits, so a session's name (`<name>-xy`) and an identifier (`<name>_cli`, `<NAME>_ROOT`) carry it. It plants no control, so the shipped workroom.bats names none of the names. Its header says it is the one arm that reads by name, and what it does not read: a listed name run into a longer word, such as a daemon's `<name>d`, and, in a tree without the list, any name.

Touched besides the tests: README.md, docs/migration.md, docs/configuration.md, .github/workflows/tests.yml, CHANGELOG.md and RELEASES/.

- **Done when 1.** workroom.bats's arm "no shipped line names a project on the workroom's list of unshipped names, in any case, inside a session's name or an identifier too, and the list does not ship (0242)" scans every file `_workroom_files` reads from tests/shipped.paths, the release notes among them, and finds none. Checked again at the bank's tip with `git grep -n -i -I -E` over the specs of tests/shipped.paths, for each listed name between characters that are not letters or digits: no line.
- **Done when 2.** The arm reads the shipped selection through `_workroom_files`, the reader every workroom arm uses, and `_workroom_hits` writes each hit as path:line:text, which its failure prints, path made relative. It holds bin/devbin among the selection, so the listing is the shipped tree, and refuses a selection that takes in intent/llm/unshipped-names, which is outside tests/shipped.paths. In a tree that tracks nothing under intent/, as the public one is, it skips, saying it read no list of unshipped names and so checked no shipped line for one; a tree that tracks intent/ and has no list fails as a workroom that has lost its list, and a list that does not read as one name a line fails too.
- **Done when 3.** Each replacement keeps its comment's technical reason, and each renamed fixture keeps its arm's verdict; vc reads the replacements in the diff.
- **Done when 4.** The landing suite: C's arms phase, in estate slot 01M61TNPWJTZMYNDBPTEZZ54ZG on molt-vc's grant, ran every arm tagged with one of the bank's eight issues on main 09c7d61a, file by file, from 2026-10-28 18:00Z to 18:08Z: in the red clone f4b30a50, main's lib with the bank's tests, under BSD; then at the bank's tip 53c92332 under BSD, and again with GNU coreutils, findutils, sed and grep first on PATH (~/Devel/scratch/devbin-cc/s5e/runs/arms/, summary in s5e/arms.out). 0242's arm failed in the red clone and passed under BSD and GNU. C was stopped on hv's word in its light phase, so its whole-file legs, the tree scans among them, did not finish; hv's runs on main took them over. No later fix touched its code. hv's `dvb test all` on rhadamanth at 217adf65 ran every one of the 2777 tests bats counts in tests/unit once, and none failed (tmp/test/20261029-0817.bats.out, its .errors empty). K0116B, the full suite on kovacs at 4d1a76b0 with rustup's cargo first on PATH, as on CI's Ubuntu runner, is green, as vc read its seal. CI run 40851772728 on 4d1a76b0 and CI run 40860048152 on 25175386, the head 0.1.16 was cut from, are green on Test on Ubuntu, Shell Script Analysis and Test Summary. No critic leg ran on the landed commits.

- **CI:** run 40860048152 on the pushed head 25175386, which carries the landing, read green by vc.
